messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

Claims:
1. "ZDDA learns from the task-irrelevant dual-domain pairs when the task-relevant target-domain training data is unavailable." -- cites: E1 (Figure 1): quote "ZDDA learns from the task-irrelevant dual-domain pairs when the task-relevant target-domain training data is unavailable."

Cited evidence:
[E1] (figure, Figure 1, page 2) (image attached): Fig. 1. We propose zero-shot deep domain adaptation (ZDDA) for domain adapta- tion and sensor fusion. ZDDA learns from the task-irrelevant dual-domain pairs when the task-relevant target-domain training data is unavailable. In this example domain adaptation task (MNIST [27] → MNIST-M [13]), the task-irrelevant gray-RGB pairs are from the Fashion-MNIST [46] dataset and the Fashion-MNIST-M dataset (the colored version of the Fashion-MNIST [46] dataset with the details in Sec. 4.1)
Words printed in the figure: 2 K.-C. Peng, Z. Wu, and J. Ernst [image]

verdicts.reason: The cited evidence (Figure 1 caption) explicitly states: 'ZDDA learns from the task-irrelevant dual-domain pairs when the task-relevant target-domain training data is unavailable.'
